# SharedUpside

<!-- generated by scripts/render.mjs from data/ ; do not edit -->

Weekly-cycle draw over every application's FWAT skim, funded by `RewardSplitter`'s         shared-upside leg. Weight accrues per application per cycle from settlement spend;         `checkpoint` closes a finished cycle and requests a VRF-selected winner weighted by that         cycle's activity, paid the configured share of the cycle's pot.

**Address**: [`0x0c5cBf7bE69c77ee8802b6Db377f17189b417Bc2`](https://evm.now/address/0x0c5cBf7bE69c77ee8802b6Db377f17189b417Bc2?chainId=1)
**Source**: `src/midway/SharedUpside.sol`

| --- | --- |
| `abandonPendingCycle(uint256)` | Give up on a pending cycle's randomness: clears the pending slot, returns the         reserved pot to `drawablePot()`, and marks the cycle `Abandoned`. The cycle's first         randomness request must be at least `cycle.vrfRetryDelay` old for either caller; a         non-owner additionally waits until `ABANDON_AFTER` has elapsed past the cycle's end. |

| `checkpoint(uint256)` | Closes `cycleId` if it has ended, requesting a VRF-selected winner over its recorded         weight. No-op while `drawsEnabled` is false: there is nothing to close yet. |
| `claimAward(uint256)` | Migrates a cycle's award into the winning application's `SharedUpsideAward` pot.         `RewardVault.payout` later resolves and pays the current recipient off that pot. |
| `enableDraws()` | Turns on cycle closes. Owner, one way. Schedules cycle 1's close at the next boundary         after this call, using cycle 1's currently configured interval; cycle 2 onward closes         on that same interval going forward. |

<details>
<summary>`abandonPendingCycle(uint256)`</summary>

The recovery for a subscription that was deleted, drained, or dropped this contract as a      consumer while a request was in flight. Without it `pendingCycleId` never clears, every      later `checkpoint` reverts `PendingRandomness`, and the reserved pot is stranded.      A callback that arrives afterward is rejected by `fulfillRandomness`'s      `pendingCycleId != cycleId` check, so the pot cannot be paid twice.Both legs are anchored on values no caller can move: `firstRequestedAt` is written once      and `cycleEnd` is fixed. `requestedAt` is not usable here because `retryRandomness` is      permissionless and rewrites it, so a gate keyed to it can be held shut by one retry per      `vrfRetryDelay`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`enableDraws()`</summary>

Before this call `cycleAt` pins every post-genesis timestamp to cycle 1, so any interval      schedule entry queued for cycle 2 or later was never reachable; it is discarded and      replaced with the one computed here.

</details>

### View

| Function | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| `ABANDON_AFTER()` | Time after a cycle ends before `abandonPendingCycle` opens to anyone. Seven days is         `_validateConfig`'s ceiling on `vrfRetryDelay`, so at least one full retry interval         fits inside it under every valid configuration. Measured from `cycleEnd`, which is         fixed: `cycle.requestedAt` moves on every `retryRandomness`, and that call is         permissionless, so a deadline keyed to it could be pushed back indefinitely. |
| `EMPTY_POT_SKIP_GRACE()` | Time after a cycle ends before `checkpoint` will skip it for nothing drawable. Inside         the grace period the call reverts `EmptyDrawablePot` instead, so a checkpoint landing         in the gap between the cycle's end and a pending funding conversion cannot burn the         cycle's draw. One day, well inside the shortest supported funding cadence and short         enough that a genuinely unfunded cycle still clears the cursor promptly. |

<details>
<summary>`cycleAt(uint256)`</summary>

Cycle 1 spans `genesisStart` to `cycleStart(2)` as a single span, not a multiple of the      genesis interval schedule's interval: while `drawsEnabled` is false there is no      `cycleStart(2)` yet, so any post-genesis timestamp is cycle 1; once `enableDraws` sets      `cycleStart(2)`, every timestamp before it is still cycle 1 regardless of how many      genesis intervals it spans. Modulo arithmetic over the interval schedule applies only      from cycle 2 onward, where cycles recur on a fixed interval from a fixed start.

</details>
